name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced

   225	    (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)

   231	    @Equiv.subsingleton _ _ (picEtAffineEquiv C A).toEquiv hplus
   232	  exact ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩
   233	
   234	end Local
   235	
   236	/-! ## The pointwise form: a hypothesis at each prime, no cover supplied
   237	
   238	The reductions above take the covering family as an argument, which is the wrong interface for
   239	a consumer: a lane computing `Pic` locally knows something *at each prime*, not a finite cover.
   240	This section removes the cover from the statement.  Two elementary steps do it, and both are
   241	about `Spec` rather than about the curve:

   243	* if a set of elements meets the complement of every prime, it generates the unit ideal
   244	  (otherwise it sits inside a maximal ideal);
   245	* the unit ideal is spanned by a **finite** subset (`Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`), which is
   246	  the compactness of `Spec A` in the form the sheaf property wants.
   247

   249	has to be threaded through the statement either. -/

   251	section Pointwise
   252	
   253	/-- A set of ring elements whose basic opens cover `Spec A` generates the unit ideal.
   254	
   255	Elementary and stated at this generality because the covering hypothesis below produces exactly
   256	this shape; a set contained in no prime is contained in no maximal ideal, hence is not proper. -/
   257	theorem span_eq_top_of_forall_prime {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (s : Set A)
   258	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f ∈ s, f ∉ p.asIdeal) :
   259	    Ideal.span s = ⊤ := by
   260	  by_contra hne
   261	  obtain ⟨m, hm, hle⟩ := Ideal.exists_le_maximal _ hne
   262	  obtain ⟨f, hfs, hf⟩ := h ⟨m, hm.isPrime⟩
   263	  exact hf (hle (Ideal.subset_span hfs))
   264	
   265	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   266	
   267	/-- **THE POINTWISE REDUCTION**: if every prime of `A` has *some* basic open neighbourhood on
   268	which the plus construction is trivial, it is trivial at `A`.
   269	
   270	No covering family in the statement: the witnesses are chosen at the primes, shown to span,
   271	cut down to a finite subfamily by `Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`, and fed to
   272	`PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away`.  This is the interface a lane computing `Pic` over local rings
   273	should target. -/
   274	theorem PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime
   275	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   276	      Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
   277	    Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) := by
   278	  classical
   279	  choose f hf hsub using h
   280	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
   281	    span_eq_top_of_forall_prime _ fun p => ⟨f p, ⟨p, rfl⟩, hf p⟩
   282	  obtain ⟨t, hts, ht⟩ := (Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite (Set.range f)).mp hspan
   283	  refine PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away C (ι := {x // x ∈ t}) (fun i => i.1)
   284	    (fun i => Localization.Away i.1) ?_ ?_
   285	  · rwa [show (Set.range fun i : {x // x ∈ t} => i.1) = (↑t : Set A) from by
   286	      ext x; exact ⟨fun ⟨i, hi⟩ => hi ▸ i.2, fun hx => ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, rfl⟩⟩]
   287	  · intro i
   288	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hts i.2

   290	
   291	/-- The pointwise reduction on the `pic⁰` carrier the producers consume. -/
   292	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime
   293	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   294	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   295	      Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
   296	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by
   297	  haveI hplus : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) :=
   298	    PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime C h
   299	  haveI : Subsingleton (picEt C (overSpec k A)) :=
   300	    @Equiv.subsingleton _ _ (picEtAffineEquiv C A).toEquiv hplus
   301	  exact ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩
   302	
   303	/-- **THE POINTWISE REDUCTION, rigidity spelling**: the `hrigAff` clause at a basic open around
   304	each prime gives it at `A`.
   305	
   306	Same three steps as `PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime` (choose, span, cut to finite), fed
   307	to `PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away`.  Stated separately because `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`
   308	consumes the rigidity clause and not a `Subsingleton`, and because the rigidity form is the one
   309	that carries no degree apparatus. -/
   310	theorem PicEtAff.rigidity_of_forall_prime
   311	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   312	      ∀ q : PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f),
   313	        (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : Localization.Away f →ₐ[k] K),
   314	          PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1)
   315	    (q : PicEtAff C A)
   316	    (hq : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : A →ₐ[k] K),
   317	      PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) :
   318	    q = 1 := by
   319	  classical
   320	  choose f hf hrig using h
   321	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
   322	    span_eq_top_of_forall_prime _ fun p => ⟨f p, ⟨p, rfl⟩, hf p⟩
   323	  obtain ⟨t, hts, ht⟩ := (Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite (Set.range f)).mp hspan
   324	  refine PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away C (ι := {x // x ∈ t}) (fun i => i.1)
   325	    (fun i => Localization.Away i.1) ?_ ?_ q hq
   326	  · rwa [show (Set.range fun i : {x // x ∈ t} => i.1) = (↑t : Set A) from by
   327	      ext x; exact ⟨fun ⟨i, hi⟩ => hi ▸ i.2, fun hx => ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, rfl⟩⟩]
   328	  · intro i
   329	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hts i.2
   330	    exact hp ▸ hrig p
   331	
   332	end Pointwise
   333	
   334	/-! ## The composition to the goal object
   335	
   336	The reductions above are worth nothing if they do not reach `JacobianData`.  These two
   337	declarations are that check, and they are what makes this file usable by the representability
   338	headline rather than local to its own row: the *pointwise-local* hypothesis, quantified over
   339	every test algebra, produces the datum through the landed producers with no atlas, no chart
   340	certificate, no coverage clause, no divisor representability and no rational point.
   341	
   342	Both carry the genus-`0` hypothesis of the producer they compose with, and neither adds anything
   343	else. -/
   344	
   345	section Datum
   346	
   347	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   348	
   349	/-- **`JacobianData` from the pointwise-local vanishing.**
   350	
   351	`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime` at every test algebra, fed to
   352	`jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` (`Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean:269`).  The
   353	hypothesis mentions no test object, no open and no morphism of schemes: only `k`-algebras, their
   354	primes, and the plus construction at the canonical localizations. -/
   355	def jacobianData_of_forall_prime_subsingleton
   356	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
   357	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   358	        Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
   359	    JacobianData C :=
   360	  jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton C fun A _ _ =>
   361	    subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime C (h A)
   362	
   363	/-- **`JacobianData` from the pointwise-local rigidity**, at genus `0`.
   364	
   365	The rigidity analogue, through `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`
   366	(`Pic0RigidityAffineReduction.lean:190`).  This is the shortest statement of the whole vanishing
   367	route's remaining debt: a local computation of the plus construction at each prime of each test
   368	algebra, and nothing else. -/
   369	def jacobianData_of_forall_prime_rigidity (hg : genus C = 0)
   370	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
   371	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   372	        ∀ q : PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f),
   373	          (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : Localization.Away f →ₐ[k] K),
   374	            PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1) :
   375	    JacobianData C :=
   376	  jacobianData_of_rigidityAff C hg fun A _ _ => PicEtAff.rigidity_of_forall_prime C (h A)

    11	
    12	The affine étale Picard functor `PicEtAff C ·` is a separated presheaf for the Zariski
    13	topology of affine tests: two plus classes over `A` agreeing on every member of a finite
    14	basic-open cover of `Spec A` agree (`AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq`).

    17	on each localization agree on an étale cover assembled from the local witnessing covers,
    18	and the finite product of the witnessing carriers is again an étale cover of the base.
    19	The gluing across the factors of the product is the relative Picard decomposition of a

    44	/-- Unfolding an equality of restrictions of two plus classes along two algebra maps
    45	into a common test algebra `R`: the descent-class representatives admit refinement maps
    46	into a common étale cover of `R`, semilinear over the restriction maps, with equal
    47	transports of the underlying relative Picard classes. -/
    48	theorem exists_relPicAlgMap_eq_of_mapAlg_eq {A₁ A₂ R : Type u}

    50	    (φ₁ : A₁ →ₐ[k] R) (φ₂ : A₂ →ₐ[k] R)

    54	    ∃ (H : Algebra.EtaleCover R) (m₁ : E₁.Carrier →ₐ[k] H.Carrier)

    57	        ∧ (∀ a : A₂, m₂ (algebraMap A₂ E₂.Carrier a) = algebraMap R H.Carrier (φ₂ a))

    92	variable (S : ι → Type u) [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra k (S i)]
    93	  [∀ i, Algebra A (S i)] [∀ i, IsScalarTower k A (S i)]
    94	  [∀ i, IsLocalization.Away (g i) (S i)]
    95	
    96	/-- A finite covering family of localizations assembles the local étale covers into an
    97	étale cover of the base: the product of the carriers. -/
    98	theorem exists_etaleCover_pi (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
    99	    (K : ∀ i, Algebra.EtaleCover (S i)) :
   100	    ∃ W : Algebra.EtaleCover A, Nonempty (W.Carrier ≃ₐ[A] Π i, (K i).Carrier) := by
   101	  classical
   102	  haveI : ∀ i, Algebra.Etale A (S i) := fun i =>
   103	    Algebra.Etale.of_isLocalizationAway (g i)
   104	  haveI : ∀ i, Algebra.Etale A (K i).Carrier := fun i =>

   108	      (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (Π i, (K i).Carrier))) := by

   142	  -- reduce to triviality of the ratio

   150	  -- unfold each local triviality to a refinement witness
   151	  have hloc : ∀ i, ∃ (K : Algebra.EtaleCover (S i)) (m : G.Carrier →ₐ[k] K.Carrier),

   155	    intro i

   157	        = mapAlg C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A (S i))
   158	            (mk C (.self A) (1 : descentClasses C (.self A))) := by

   164	    · exact hm₁ a

   166	        relPic C (overSpec k (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).Carrier)) = 1 from rfl,

   182	      show (Pi.evalAlgHom k (fun j => (K j).Carrier) i).comp
   183	          (Pi.algHom k (fun j => (K j).Carrier) (fun j => m j))

   187	  have hW : relPicAlgMap C
   188	      ((e.symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k).comp
   189	        (Pi.algHom k (fun j => (K j).Carrier) (fun j => m j)))
   190	      (ζ : relPic C (overSpec k G.Carrier)) = 1 := by
   191	    rw [relPicAlgMap_comp, hpi, map_one]
   192	  -- the joint refinement map is an `A`-algebra map
   193	  have hcommA : ∀ a : A,
   194	      ((e.symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k).comp
   195	        (Pi.algHom k (fun j => (K j).Carrier) (fun j => m j)))

   197	    intro a
   198	    have h1 : (Pi.algHom k (fun j => (K j).Carrier) (fun j => m j))
   199	        (algebraMap A G.Carrier a) = algebraMap A (Π j, (K j).Carrier) a := by

   201	      exact hmA j a
